items.label: BESI Q1 FY2026 (04-23-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Hybrid-bonding LOGIC acceleration: HB unit orders MORE THAN

set.signal: Hybrid-bonding LOGIC acceleration: HB unit orders MORE THAN DOUBLED QoQ and exceeded the prior quarterly peak (Q2 2024) in both total units and order value. CEO: the Taiwan customer's order scheduled for installation in the first round in AP7 was pulled forward somewhat from Q2 to Q1, and the program was enlarged - the anticipated 100 bonders - 'we are told' - 'may be significantly higher', plus orders placed for co-packaged optics. Adopters named by the CEO: AMD (the first, several families), Broadcom, the Apple M5, and roadmaps from 'another very big customer in the data center modules'; HB adoption now 20 customers (18 a quarter ago). TCB Next: 2 new orders, adoption at six customers. US: the big round for the initial HB capacity was received about 1.5 years ago and is being filled in, qualified and tested - more bonders depend on that customer's adoption. Intel EMIB: BESI has been involved 'since the very beginning in placement of these EMIB modules' and delivered the systems for Intel's significant installed capacity; rising EMIB demand 'could be a positive business impact, but as things with Intel develop as they do, we first need to see more evidence'.
set.figure: HB orders >2x QoQ (new peak); AP7 pulled forward; 100 bonders 'may be significantly higher'; 20 HB customers

items.label: BESI Q1 FY2026 (04-23-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Q1 2026: revenue EUR 184.9M (+28.3% YoY) on higher shipments

set.signal: Q1 2026: revenue EUR 184.9M (+28.3% YoY) on higher shipments for high-end mobile and 2.5D AI photonics and data center applications; ORDERS EUR 269.7M (more than doubled YoY, +7.7% QoQ); net income +63.8% YoY, net margin 27.9% (vs 21.9%); GM 63.5% (increased prices offset component and energy cost inflation); net cash +186.9% QoQ to EUR 103.3M on EUR 93M cash flow from operations (more than doubled YoY). Guidance: Q2 revenue +30%-40% QoQ with GM rising to 64%-66%, opex flat to up 10% -> H1 2026 revenue +49% vs H1 2025 at the midpoint of the Q2 guidance. Market: the latest TechInsights forecast calls for 21% assembly market growth in 2026 and 75% between 2025 and 2030 - BESI expects to SIGNIFICANTLY EXCEED those rates on its advanced-packaging leadership (flip chip, multi-module die attach, hybrid bonding, next-generation TCB).
set.figure: Orders EUR 269.7M (more than doubled YoY); GM 63.5% -> 64-66% guide; H1 rev +49%

items.label: BESI Q1 FY2026 (04-23-2026)
items.signal_prefix: China & new form factors: several robust orders from Chinese

set.signal: China & new form factors: several robust orders from Chinese-based customers - 2.5D CoWoS-like capacity expansion, photonics pluggables, a recovery in high-end smartphone modules; China is engaged in developing hybrid bonding, possibly in 3D stacking 'to lengthen the node size life' because it is not allowed to invest in a next generation with smaller device geometry - 'could be a very significant market'; BESI itself is developing such modules, 'still in very early stage', with end applications 'still distant'; the current big China market is 2.5D mass reflow flip chip; BESI sells only what the regulations allow (US government rules, tested every six months). Capacity moving outside China: Malaysia, Philippines, Thailand and Vietnam (BESI's Vietnam facility is building tools, its first bonding system - not hybrid - by the end of this year, freeing Malaysia capacity for wafer-level assembly) and India (five major customers setting up production, mostly power devices). PANEL: the 310 by 310 panel is coming to market in the next year and 2 years - BESI already received orders for certain applications and its bonders can handle 310 by 310 (hybrid on panel 'a bit early'). Photonics: next-generation pluggables require more bonding steps; for the CPO process BESI 'delivered the hybrid bonding for accomplishing those kinds of contacts'.

items.label: BESI Q1 FY2026 (04-23-2026)
items.signal_prefix: CEO: all three memory makers now have BESI hybrid bonders to

set.signal: CEO: all three memory makers now have BESI hybrid bonders to evaluate and define the adoption of hybrid bonding for HBM stacking - repeat orders from a memory customer for HBM applications; a Korean customer that started a lab program ('I think') two years ago has moved it to the forefront, with two applications (logic and HBM stacking); 2 evaluation tools shipped to the third memory maker (a full tool-of-record evaluation, the CEO confirmed). All three are evaluating for 'one specific end customer' that 'has invited all three to have these hybrid bonded stacks available by the end of 2026 to be used in end market applications in 2027'. Timeline: 2026 is 'a major qualification year' (the first customer aiming at June/July, the second 'a bit following behind', which 'could be end of Q3, Q4'), and - based on the success of the qualification - production capabilities set up towards the end of the year for mainstream volume production in 2027. The CEO said the rule of thumb of 150 hybrid bonding systems for logic implying an HBM TAM of 600 'still stands' (a processor carries 3 or 4 memory stacks; a stack of 16 dies needs 16 bonds versus one logic device). For HBM he expects integrated lines (with Applied Materials' Kinex) rather than standalone, because HBM is dedicated high-volume production; the bonder's value to BESI is the same standalone or integrated. A possible relaxation of the JEDEC thickness standards 'does not change the advantage of using a hybrid process over a reflow process' (only one of the three needs that height). Yields: a process must be 'well up into the 99.9%'; logic hybrid bonding yields are 'very well up in the 99.99%', for HBM stacking 'one still has to prove that'.
